questions.prompt: How is Peter's description of himself as a failure qualified?
questions.promptZh: Peter把自己说成失败者时，有什么限定？
options: It is given as an objective rating of every part of his life.
It is limited by the phrase 'in some sense' within the literary quotation.
It is presented as Sally's direct accusation, rather than Peter's reflection.
It says Peter had never held any belief or ambition.
optionsZh: 它是对人生每方面的客观评分。
文学引语中的in some sense对它加了限定。
它是Sally直接指责，而非Peter反思。
它说Peter从没有任何信念或志向。
analyses: A some sense不是所有方面，也非客观量表。
B 小说人物谈自身失败的引语保留某种意义上的限定，不扩大为整个人生全面失败。
C Peter Walsh talks about his own failure标明归属，不能移给Sally。
D had been a Socialist承认过去身份，不能改成从无信念或志向。

vocabulary.meaning: 在某种意义上；从某个角度说
vocabulary.context: 限定failure的判断范围，不等于在所有维度都失败或已客观测得。
vocabulary.example: He regarded himself as a failure in some sense, not in every respect.

questions.evidenceQuote: When I read Mrs. Dalloway, I was Clarissa Dalloway and Peter Walsh’s age. That made it easy to identify with those characters: all the obligations of daily life, ennui, and the past obsessions and obsession with the past. Peter Walsh talks about his own failure, saying, “He had been a Socialist, in some sense a failure—true.

questions.prompt: In the quoted thought, whose hands hold the future of civilisation?
questions.promptZh: 引述的想法认为文明未来掌握在谁手中？
options: Older men precisely because they have stopped reading.
People who reject abstract principles and every book.
The booksellers alone, rather than the people reading their books.
Young men like his younger self, interested in principles, science, and philosophy.
optionsZh: 年长者，因为他们停止阅读。
拒绝抽象原则和所有书籍的人。
只有书商，而非读书的人。
像他年轻时那样热爱原则、科学和哲学的青年。
analyses: A young men是明确对象，不能倒成年长且停止读书。
B love of abstract principles与reading science/philosophy都与拒绝相反。
C 伦敦送书为青年读书的说明，不把未来归给书商。
D in the hands of young men...such as he was thirty years ago给群体与比较；这是小说人物的思考，不是未来已证实结果。

vocabulary.meaning: 在于；掌握于；处于某种归属
vocabulary.context: 未来lies in the hands是比喻表达，非身体躺卧，也非说谎的lies。
vocabulary.example: In his view, the future lies in the hands of curious young people.

questions.evidenceQuote: Still the future of civilisation lies, he thought, in the hands of young men like that; of young men such as he was, thirty years ago; with their love of abstract principles; getting books sent out to them all the way from London to a peak in the Himalayas; reading science; reading philosophy.” At the end of the party, Sally, Clarissa’s close friend in adolescence who used to deride Richard, Clarissa’s husband, as not smart enough, says, “Richard has improved. You are right. I shall go and talk to him.

questions.prompt: What does 'I shall say good-night' express?
questions.promptZh: I shall say good-night表达什么？
options: The speaker's intention to offer a farewell.
Proof that the farewell has already been completed.
A command requiring every guest to leave immediately.
A denial that the speaker plans to say anything.
optionsZh: 说话者打算道晚安告别。
证明告别已经完成。
命令所有来客立即离开。
否认说话者打算说任何话。
analyses: A shall在这里以第一人称表达将要做的事，say good-night为告别。
B 将来意向不是已完成事件，句中未说已经说完。
C 主语I，未命令every guest。
D shall say是肯定意向，非否认开口。

vocabulary.meaning: 将；这里表达第一人称的意向
vocabulary.context: 此处不能改作已经完成，亦非对网站用户下命令。
vocabulary.example: The speaker says that she shall say good-night.

questions.evidenceQuote: I shall say good-night. What does the brain matter…compared with the heart?” Old Peter, in the end, reflects, “What is this terror? What is this ecstasy?…What is it that fills me with extraordinary excitement?”

questions.prompt: How is the question about terror presented?
questions.promptZh: 关于terror的问句以什么方式呈现？
options: As Sally's stated assessment of Richard's intelligence.
As an instruction telling Peter which feelings he must have.
As old Peter's reflection on his own emotional experience.
As an objectively verified physical attack at the party.
optionsZh: Sally对Richard智力的评价。
指示Peter必须有什么感受。
年长Peter对自身情绪体验的自问。
聚会上经客观证实的身体袭击。
analyses: A 前句brain/heart属于Sally话语，本问由Old Peter...reflects另行引出。
B reflects为反思，不是别人命令其必须感觉怎样。
C Peter对感受自问，保留文学人物的内心归属。
D terror在情绪追问中不足以证明发生外部袭击。

vocabulary.meaning: 沉思；反思；向内思考
vocabulary.context: 这里引出Peter对感受的内心追问，不是镜面反光或一项实验记录。
vocabulary.example: Peter reflects on the emotions that fill him with excitement.

questions.evidenceQuote: I shall say good-night. What does the brain matter…compared with the heart?” Old Peter, in the end, reflects, “What is this terror? What is this ecstasy?…What is it that fills me with extraordinary excitement?”

questions.prompt: What does 'ecstasy' convey in the paired questions?
questions.promptZh: 成对问句中的ecstasy传达什么？
options: A calm indifference with almost no emotional response.
An intense feeling of delight or rapture alongside the passage's other strong emotion.
A mild satisfaction that rules out extraordinary excitement.
Fear alone, with no positive or exhilarating feeling.
optionsZh: 几乎无情绪反应的平静冷漠。
强烈喜悦或狂喜，与段落另一强烈情绪并置。
排除极度激动的轻微满意。
只有害怕，没有任何积极或兴奋感。
analyses: A ecstasy和extraordinary excitement不支持冷漠。
B 与terror并列，并有extraordinary excitement，突出强烈而复杂的情绪；不据此下临床诊断。
C ecstasy的强度远超轻微，extraordinary也不能删去。
D 将ecstasy读成只有恐惧，抹掉它的狂喜义及与terror的并置。

vocabulary.meaning: 狂喜；极强烈的喜悦或出神感
vocabulary.context: 在小说内心追问中描述情绪，与terror同现，不宜直接推成病名或化学药物含义。
vocabulary.example: The character wonders about a feeling of ecstasy and excitement.

questions.evidenceQuote: I shall say good-night. What does the brain matter…compared with the heart?” Old Peter, in the end, reflects, “What is this terror? What is this ecstasy?…What is it that fills me with extraordinary excitement?”

questions.prompt: What contrast does the description of Peter emphasise?
questions.promptZh: 对Peter的描述强调什么反差？
options: He has no education or travel experience, so his uncertainty is unsurprising.
He knows exactly what he wants because all educated people must do so.
He is uneducated but has already written many successful novels.
He is educated and well travelled yet remains unsure what he wants from life.
optionsZh: 他没受教育也没旅行，所以茫然并不意外。
他完全知道所求，因为所有有教育者都必然如此。
他没受教育但已写许多成功小说。
他教育良好、游历丰富，却仍不清楚人生所求。
analyses: A well-educated、well-traveled明确肯定，两项都被倒置。
B truly clueless与完全清楚相反，教育未被写成充分保证。
C 他在引述里答Not a word，不支持多部成功作品。
D For...truly clueless呈现经历丰富与人生目标茫然之间的张力，是作者对人物的解读。

vocabulary.meaning: 茫然的；不知道该怎样理解或选择的
vocabulary.context: as to what he wants限定不清楚人生所求，不等于从未学过任何知识。
vocabulary.example: Despite his experience, he remained clueless about what he wanted.
collocations: clueless as to what he wants

questions.evidenceQuote: For a well-educated and well-traveled person, Peter is truly clueless as to what he wants in his life. When he was young, he thought he would be a writer. Sally asked, “Have you written?” Peter replied, at age fifty-two, “Not a word!” and laughed.

questions.prompt: What does Sally's question check against Peter's earlier ambition?
questions.promptZh: Sally的问句对照Peter早年志向，核问什么？
options: Whether he has actually written anything after once expecting to be a writer.
Whether he has ever visited India as a tourist.
Whether Clarissa has written a biography of him.
Whether he intends to become a writer only after Sally's question.
optionsZh: 既然曾以为会成为作家，他是否实际写过东西。
他是否曾以游客身份去印度。
Clarissa是否给他写了传记。
他是否只在Sally提问后才打算当作家。
analyses: A When he was young...would be a writer在前，Have you written追问是否付诸写作。
B 问句动词written，没有问旅行。
C 主语you对Peter发问，非问Clarissa传记。
D 志向在young时已有，不能改成此次提问才首次出现。

vocabulary.meaning: 你写过吗；询问到当前是否已有写作成果
vocabulary.context: 在本段连接早年作家想象与后来实际经历，不问未来打算本身。
vocabulary.example: Sally asks whether he has written anything.

questions.evidenceQuote: For a well-educated and well-traveled person, Peter is truly clueless as to what he wants in his life. When he was young, he thought he would be a writer. Sally asked, “Have you written?” Peter replied, at age fifty-two, “Not a word!” and laughed.

questions.prompt: Who laughs in the continuation after the reply?
questions.promptZh: 回答后紧接的and laughed是谁笑了？
options: Sally, who laughs before asking her question.
Clarissa, who interrupts to answer on Peter's behalf.
Peter, after replying that he has not written a word.
The narrator, while reporting a real interview with the novelist.
optionsZh: Sally在发问前笑。
Clarissa打断并代Peter回答。
Peter答一字没写后笑。
叙述者报道与小说家真实访谈时笑。
analyses: A and laughed接Peter replied及其引语，未把动作归Sally或移到发问前。
B 无Clarissa打断代答。
C 连词and继续同一Peter的动作；原候选边界把它分出，完整段落仍保留正确附着。
D 这是文学人物对话的讨论，不是作者真实访谈记录。

vocabulary.meaning: 笑了；发笑
vocabulary.context: 这里只明确动作主体与叙事顺序，不能仅凭笑就断言人物没有遗憾或对所有失败满意。
vocabulary.example: Peter replied and laughed after acknowledging that he had written nothing.

questions.evidenceQuote: For a well-educated and well-traveled person, Peter is truly clueless as to what he wants in his life. When he was young, he thought he would be a writer. Sally asked, “Have you written?” Peter replied, at age fifty-two, “Not a word!” and laughed.

questions.prompt: What range of Clarissa's life appears in Peter's thoughts?
questions.promptZh: Peter的思绪覆盖Clarissa人生的什么范围？
options: Only the single evening of the party, without earlier memories.
Only her adulthood, after he first met her in India.
Three different women who share Clarissa's name.
Her childhood, adolescence, and adulthood.
optionsZh: 只有聚会一晚，无早年记忆。
只有成年，且他在印度才初见她。
三个同名Clarissa的不同女性。
她的童年、少年与成年。
analyses: A Throughout及三个人生阶段超出单晚。
B childhood/adolescence均明列，India指他找到爱情的地方，不是此句初见Clarissa的交代。
C 重复名字聚焦同一人不同时期，未引三位同名者。
D 三阶段逐项在句中，体现思绪反复围绕同一人。

vocabulary.meaning: 贯穿；在全部所述范围内
vocabulary.context: Throughout the novel说小说全篇的反复关注，不等于每个真实人每时每刻都相同。
vocabulary.example: Throughout the novel, he returns in thought to her earlier life.

questions.evidenceQuote: Throughout the novel, Peter thinks about Clarissa, Clarissa in childhood, adolescence, and adulthood. Although he found love in India, he could not keep his eyes off her. What is so attractive about Clarissa?

questions.prompt: What does the question about Clarissa's attractiveness ask the reader to consider?
questions.promptZh: 关于Clarissa吸引力的问句要求思考什么？
options: A confirmed experimental rule explaining every person's attraction.
What accounts for Peter's persistent fascination with Clarissa.
The exact number of parties Clarissa hosted each year.
Whether Peter had entirely stopped noticing her after finding love in India.
optionsZh: 一条解释所有人吸引力的已证实实验定律。
什么能解释Peter对Clarissa持续着迷。
Clarissa每年聚会的精确场数。
Peter在印度找到爱情后是否已完全不再注意她。
analyses: A 文学人物的吸引问题不等于普遍实验规律。
B 问句承接thinks about和could not keep his eyes off her，探问持续吸引的原因。
C 当前没有计数聚会的提问。
D 上句说although...could not keep his eyes off，注意仍持续，不是全停。

vocabulary.meaning: 有吸引力的；令人着迷的
vocabulary.context: 此处不必只指外貌评分，问题来自人物长期持续的注意。
vocabulary.example: The question asks what makes Clarissa so attractive to Peter.
collocations: What is so attractive about Clarissa
could not keep his eyes off her

questions.evidenceQuote: Throughout the novel, Peter thinks about Clarissa, Clarissa in childhood, adolescence, and adulthood. Although he found love in India, he could not keep his eyes off her. What is so attractive about Clarissa?

questions.prompt: What does 'still' highlight in the description of the fifty-two-year-old man?
questions.promptZh: 描述52岁男子时，still突出什么？
options: His intense love for an old girlfriend continues at this later stage of life.
He has only just met a stranger and has no earlier connection with her.
His girlfriend is explicitly said to return his feelings to the same degree.
His age is measured as the number of years since they last spoke.
optionsZh: 到了这一人生阶段，对旧女友的强烈爱仍持续。
他才初识陌生人，与她无早年联系。
原文明说女友同样程度回爱。
年龄就是他们最后谈话后经过的年数。
analyses: A fifty-two-year-old与still...old girlfriend并置，强调旧关系对象的持续感情。
B old girlfriend否定初识陌生人的读法。
C 这里只明确男子的感情，没有给同等回应的证明。
D fifty-two-year-old给人物年龄，不是离别时长。

vocabulary.meaning: 仍然；到当前叙述时点还持续
vocabulary.context: 强调感情延续，不能据此推出对方回报同样强度或关系中所有事情都没变。
vocabulary.example: He is still deeply interested in someone he has known for years.

questions.evidenceQuote: That is largely a mystery to me. But here is a fifty-two-year-old man still madly in love with his old girlfriend. No boredom here, but pure, genuine, endless curiosity about one woman. As Offill finds a lifetime of lessons from Mrs. Dalloway, Peter keeps finding old and new appeal in Clarissa.

questions.prompt: What is contrasted with boredom in the passage?
questions.promptZh: 段落用什么与无聊对照？
options: The complete absence of interest in anyone familiar.
A measured need to replace every old relationship.
Persistent, genuine curiosity about the same woman.
Certainty that nothing remains to be discovered in Clarissa.
optionsZh: 对任何熟悉者完全无兴趣。
经测量必须更换每段旧关系。
对同一个女人持续而真切的好奇。
确信Clarissa再无可发现之处。
analyses: A curiosity和keeps finding appeal是持续兴趣，非全无。
B one woman强调同一对象，没有测量或要求换人。
C No boredom...but...curiosity给明确对照，后句旧新吸引力承接。
D endless curiosity与keeps finding old and new appeal不支持发现已尽。

vocabulary.meaning: 真切的；真诚而非假装的
vocabulary.context: 这里修饰人物好奇的质地，是作者文学解读用词，不是实验鉴真结论。
vocabulary.example: The passage describes a genuine curiosity about a familiar person.

questions.evidenceQuote: That is largely a mystery to me. But here is a fifty-two-year-old man still madly in love with his old girlfriend. No boredom here, but pure, genuine, endless curiosity about one woman. As Offill finds a lifetime of lessons from Mrs. Dalloway, Peter keeps finding old and new appeal in Clarissa.

questions.prompt: What does the passage explicitly say about the proverb?
questions.promptZh: 段落对这句谚语明确说了什么？
options: It originated exclusively in Japan, as proved by a historical study.
It is popular in Japan.
Only people unfamiliar with old works can understand it.
It requires replacing all old knowledge with unrelated new material.
optionsZh: 历史研究证明它仅起源于日本。
它在日本很常用。
只有不熟悉旧作的人能理解。
它要求以无关新材料替换所有旧知。
analyses: A popular in不等于唯一发源地，句中没有起源史研究。
B There is a popular proverb in Japan明确说明使用背景，保持其陈述范围。
C 片段未把理解限于陌生者，后文反而谈温习旧知。
D 原段联系old与new，不是舍弃全部旧知。

vocabulary.meaning: 谚语；凝练传达一般经验的常用说法
vocabulary.context: 文中说日本常用，并不据此证明发源地或所有人都遵循。
vocabulary.example: The proverb connects revisiting the old with learning something new.

questions.evidenceQuote: There is a popular proverb in Japan, 温故知新. The first character means “warm,” the second “old,” the third “knowledge,” and the last “new.” Warm the old, then you will learn something new. We often learn something new from studying something very old.

questions.prompt: Which pair matches the meanings assigned to the third and last characters?
questions.promptZh: 哪组对应文中第三个字与最后一个字的释义？
options: Warm and old.
New and knowledge.
Old and warm.
Knowledge and new.
optionsZh: 温与旧。
新与知识。
旧与温。
知识与新。
analyses: A warm/old是第一、第二字，不是所问位置。
B 使用了两个相关释义，但颠倒third与last顺序。
C 是前两个字倒序，不符third/last。
D the third knowledge、the last new直接对应，题目要求保持字位顺序。

vocabulary.meaning: 文字中的字；书写符号
vocabulary.context: 此处说四个汉字，不是小说人物、人格或电影角色。
vocabulary.example: Each character in the proverb is given a meaning.

questions.evidenceQuote: There is a popular proverb in Japan, 温故知新. The first character means “warm,” the second “old,” the third “knowledge,” and the last “new.” Warm the old, then you will learn something new. We often learn something new from studying something very old.

questions.prompt: How does the passage explain warming the old?
questions.promptZh: 段落怎样解释温习旧的？
options: Revisiting or studying old things can lead to new learning.
Old material must be physically heated before it can be read.
Everything old prevents learning and should be discarded.
New understanding is possible only by avoiding familiar works.
optionsZh: 重访或研习旧事物能带来新知。
旧材料必须实际加热后才能阅读。
所有旧物都阻止学习，须丢弃。
只有避开熟悉作品才能有新理解。
analyses: A Warm the old...learn new后接studying something very old说明温习与新知的联系。
B warm在谚语解释中不能机械当成加热操作要求。
C learn new from old与一律舍弃相反。
D 全段论熟悉与旧材料中的发现，不限定只靠陌生材料。

vocabulary.meaning: 研习；认真考察与学习
vocabulary.context: 此处学古老材料可有新发现，不只表示报读学校或机械背诵。
vocabulary.example: Studying an old work closely can reveal a new detail.

questions.evidenceQuote: There is a popular proverb in Japan, 温故知新. The first character means “warm,” the second “old,” the third “knowledge,” and the last “new.” Warm the old, then you will learn something new. We often learn something new from studying something very old.

questions.prompt: What shared pattern is attributed to the listed musicians and artists?
questions.promptZh: 列举的音乐人与艺术家被归于哪种共同模式？
options: They kept one unchanging style throughout every phase of their work.
They all worked in the same medium and produced the same number of works.
They experimented, tried new styles, and developed over time.
They avoided innovation once they had established an audience.
optionsZh: 所有创作阶段都维持唯一不变风格。
都用相同媒介、作品数也相同。
他们实验、尝试新风格，并随时间演变。
有受众之后就回避创新。
analyses: A evolved over time和new styles不支持始终唯一不变。
B 所列横跨音乐与视觉艺术，句中也未给相同产量。
C embraced experiment、tried new styles、evolved三项是破折号后的共同概括。
D embraced experiment与回避创新相反，亦无一旦成名即停止的时间条件。

vocabulary.meaning: 欣然接受；积极采纳
vocabulary.context: 在embraced experiment中指接纳实验探索，不是身体拥抱实验物件。
vocabulary.example: The artists embraced experiment and developed new styles.

questions.evidenceQuote: The Beatles, Bob Dylan, Aretha Franklin, Miles Davis, Picasso, Yayoi Kusama, Hilma af Klint, Kara Walker—all have embraced experiment, tried new styles, and evolved over time. You can learn something new from each of these artists by digging deeper and deeper into their work over a long period of time. If you don’t feel like reading, listening to, or studying something new, you might try old favorites that you haven’t engaged with for a long time. You might discover something new and rich.

questions.prompt: What route to new learning does the author describe?
questions.promptZh: 作者描述了哪条获得新知的路径？
options: Listening once and assuming that the work has been exhausted.
Studying familiar artists' work ever more deeply over a long period.
Waiting for a new release before any earlier work can reveal anything.
Counting the artists' names instead of engaging with their work.
optionsZh: 只听一次就认定作品已穷尽。
长时间不断深入研习这些艺术家的作品。
必须等待新发行，旧作才可透露新东西。
只数艺术家名字，不接触作品。
analyses: A deeper and deeper、long period与一次穷尽相反。
B by引出方式，into their work与long period分别限定对象及时间。
C 旧爱也可新发现，未要求新发行作为必要条件。
D 深入作品不是仅数名单。

vocabulary.meaning: 更深入探究；不断挖掘理解
vocabulary.context: 此处比喻作品探索，不是实际挖地，也不只指搜集更多姓名。
vocabulary.example: Digging deeper into a familiar painting can reveal details missed before.
collocations: digging deeper and deeper into their work
over a long period of time

questions.evidenceQuote: The Beatles, Bob Dylan, Aretha Franklin, Miles Davis, Picasso, Yayoi Kusama, Hilma af Klint, Kara Walker—all have embraced experiment, tried new styles, and evolved over time. You can learn something new from each of these artists by digging deeper and deeper into their work over a long period of time. If you don’t feel like reading, listening to, or studying something new, you might try old favorites that you haven’t engaged with for a long time. You might discover something new and rich.

questions.prompt: What is the new lens the author invites the reader to use?
questions.promptZh: 作者邀请读者采用的new lens是什么？
options: A single score that replaces happiness and meaning with wealth.
A way to ignore every familiar experience in favour of new travel.
A claim that a good life has only one possible dimension.
Viewing life through happiness, meaning, and psychological richness together.
optionsZh: 用财富替代快乐和意义的单一分数。
忽略所有熟悉经历，只看新旅行。
声称好人生只有唯一维度。
把快乐、意义、心理丰富一起作为看人生的视角。
analyses: A 前文列happy、meaningful与rich，并没有财富替代的公式。
B lens指概念视角，未要求舍弃所有熟悉经历。
C life in three dimensions与only one相反。
D 句中三种人生的ingredients承接new lens，表明拓展观察维度；let’s see if保留尝试的语气。

vocabulary.meaning: 视角；用来理解事物的框架
vocabulary.context: 此处为比喻，不指必须购买的相机镜片或网站视觉设置。
vocabulary.example: The three dimensions provide a new lens for considering experience.

questions.evidenceQuote: In this book, I introduced the new concept of a psychologically rich life, adding to the two better-known paths to a good life: a happy life and a meaningful life. Now that you know the ingredients of a happy life, a meaningful life, and a psychologically rich life, let’s see if you can start seeing the world through a new lens: life in three dimensions.

questions.prompt: How is the conversation in Jazz framed?
questions.promptZh: 《Jazz》中的谈话以什么叙事框架引入？
options: Violet recalls a conversation with her hairdresser near the end of the novel.
The hairdresser reports an experiment conducted with Toni Morrison.
Violet interviews real participants after finishing a psychology survey.
The narrator retells a conversation with his own hairdresser as a new event.
optionsZh: 小说近结尾时，Violet回忆与理发师的谈话。
理发师报告与Toni Morrison开展的实验。
Violet在心理问卷后访谈现实参与者。
叙述者把与自己理发师的新事重讲一遍。
analyses: A Toward the end、Violet、recalls、her hairdresser逐项对应时间位置、人物与回忆对象。
B Toni Morrison是作品作者，不是此处被报告实验的合作者。
C 是小说人物回忆，不能当现实调查材料。
D her指Violet，非作者自身；recalls也非刚发生的新事。

vocabulary.meaning: 回忆起；在心中重提过去事件
vocabulary.context: 这里是小说中的记忆框架，不能把它误作当前作者亲历或新的研究观察。
vocabulary.example: Violet recalls a conversation from earlier in her life.

questions.evidenceQuote: Toward the end of Toni Morrison’s Jazz, Violet, the main character, recalls a conversation with her hairdresser. Her hairdresser says, “What’s the world for you if you can’t make it up the way you want it?” Violet is surprised by the question; the thought had never crossed her mind. “What’s the point?

questions.prompt: What possibility does the hairdresser's question raise?
questions.promptZh: 理发师的问句提出什么可能？
options: That Violet has no role in how she thinks about her life.
That every external event is guaranteed to obey a person's wishes.
That one can imagine the world in a personally desired way.
That the world has already been objectively measured as meaningless for everyone.
optionsZh: Violet对怎样看自己人生完全无份。
每件外部事件都保证服从个人愿望。
人可以按个人想要的方式想象世界。
世界已被客观测定对所有人都无意义。
analyses: A if you can’t make it up the way you want it挑战的是如何看世界的能动性，非预设完全无份。
B 问句没有保证外部一切服从愿望，不能把想象视角扩成全能控制。
C make it up...the way you want给对自我世界的构想；这是文学对话的启发式问题。
D 非实验测量，也无for everyone的全称结论。

vocabulary.meaning: 构想；在心中把它组织成某种样子
vocabulary.context: 在这段文学对话中关涉想象世界与自我人生，不是自动保证改变一切外部事实。
vocabulary.example: The question invites her to make it up the way she wants it.
collocations: make it up the way you want it

questions.evidenceQuote: Toward the end of Toni Morrison’s Jazz, Violet, the main character, recalls a conversation with her hairdresser. Her hairdresser says, “What’s the world for you if you can’t make it up the way you want it?” Violet is surprised by the question; the thought had never crossed her mind. “What’s the point?

questions.prompt: What does 'point' mean in the short question?
questions.promptZh: 简短问句里的point是什么意思？
options: A sharp tip on a physical object.
The purpose or usefulness of doing or thinking something.
A score awarded during a game.
An exact location marked on a map.
optionsZh: 实物的尖端。
做某事或这样思考的意义、用处。
比赛得到的分数。
地图标出的精确地点。
analyses: A What’s the point是询问意义的表达，非物体尖端。
B 在围绕怎样构想人生的对话里，point为目的或价值，不能逐词套用其他义项。
C 没有比赛计分情境。
D 没有地图定位语境；候选边界在问号处截开，完整邻近对话仍在来源中保留。

vocabulary.meaning: 意义；用处；目的
vocabulary.context: What’s the point为常见询问价值的表达，不是尖端、比赛分或地图点。
vocabulary.example: She asks what the point of the proposed change would be.
collocations: the thought had never crossed her mind

Her hairdresser says, “What’s the world for you if you can’t make it up the way you want it?” Violet is surprised by the question; the thought had never crossed her mind. “What’s the point?

questions.prompt: What consequence does the author attach to not imagining the world as one wants?
questions.promptZh: 作者给不按自己所愿思考世界接上什么后果？
options: Forgetting that it is one's own life.
Losing the ability to remember any factual event.
Guaranteeing that every wish will come true without action.
Proving that only happiness can matter in a good life.
optionsZh: 忘记这是自己的人生。
失去记住任何事实事件的能力。
保证不用行动愿望也全实现。
证明好人生只能在乎快乐。
analyses: A If...you forget it is your life直接给条件和所述后果，是作者的反思性论述。
B forget的宾语是it is your life，不是医学性全记忆损失。
C 句中没有愿望必实现的保证。
D 后续还列意义与丰富，不能限为只有快乐。

vocabulary.meaning: 忘记；忽略或不再意识到
vocabulary.context: 这里指忽略自己对人生的主体位置，不是诊断记忆障碍。
vocabulary.example: The passage warns that people may forget it is their own life.
collocations: think of the world the way you want it

questions.evidenceQuote: If you don’t think of the world the way you want it, you forget it is your life. So, let us not forget that this is our life and that we want something more than what it is. Maybe more happiness, more meaning, or more psychological richness. Instead of waiting until you’ve reached your deathbed, perhaps try to reflect after each milestone: What would you say about your high school life at the end of high school?

questions.prompt: What does 'So, let us not forget' ask the reader to retain?
questions.promptZh: So,let us not forget要求读者记住什么？
options: That all desires must be abandoned once a milestone is reached.
That the present state is the only possible form of one's life.
That a good life can be judged only at death and never earlier.
That this is our life and we want something beyond its present state.
optionsZh: 一到重要节点就得放弃所有愿望。
现状是人生唯一可能形式。
只能临终评价人生，不能更早。
这是自己的人生，而且想要比现状更多的东西。
analyses: A 原句want something more，非放弃所有愿望。
B more than what it is为超出现状留空间。
C 下句建议节点反思而非等临终，方向相反。
D 两个that并列人生归属与求更多的愿望；So承接前句提醒，不把愿望等同已实现。

vocabulary.meaning: 更多一些的东西；超出现状的追求
vocabulary.context: 后面列可能是快乐、意义或丰富，当前表达不保证每项都能无限增加。
vocabulary.example: They want something more than the present form of their life.
collocations: something more than what it is

questions.evidenceQuote: If you don’t think of the world the way you want it, you forget it is your life. So, let us not forget that this is our life and that we want something more than what it is. Maybe more happiness, more meaning, or more psychological richness. Instead of waiting until you’ve reached your deathbed, perhaps try to reflect after each milestone: What would you say about your high school life at the end of high school?

questions.prompt: How does the fragment beginning with 'Maybe' develop the previous sentence?
questions.promptZh: Maybe开头的片段怎样展开前句？
options: It insists that only money counts as something more.
It says the three dimensions must all rise equally for every person.
It suggests happiness, meaning, or psychological richness as possible forms of the desired 'more'.
It rejects all three dimensions as irrelevant to the reader's life.
optionsZh: 坚持更多只能是金钱。
说三维对每人都必须等幅增长。
把快乐、意义或心理丰富列为所求更多的可能形式。
把三维都排除出读者人生。
analyses: A 所列为三个人生维度，非only money。
B Maybe和or保留可能与选择，未要求每人等幅增加。
C 这一名词性片段补充something more的具体可能，不伪造独立的完整主谓句。
D 明确列举用于展开，不是全部否定。

vocabulary.meaning: 也许；提出可能而非确定要求
vocabulary.context: 与or合用给潜在方向，不能改成人人必须同时最大化三维。
vocabulary.example: Maybe the desired change is more meaning rather than more comfort.
collocations: more meaning, or more psychological richness

questions.prompt: Which milestone is the question asking the reader to use for reviewing college life?
questions.promptZh: 这句问读者用哪个节点回顾大学生活？
options: The start of primary school.
The end of college.
Only the last day of life.
The end of a child's high-school education instead of one's own college period.
optionsZh: 小学开始。
大学结束。
只有临终日。
孩子高中毕业，而非自己的大学阶段。
analyses: A college不等于primary school。
B your college life at the end of college明确将回顾对象与阶段终点对应。
C 问的是较早人生节点，非只等临终。
D parenting/child高中毕业是片段里的另一例，不能替换当前大学回顾节点。

vocabulary.meaning: 在……结束时；阶段终点
vocabulary.context: 这里将大学经历与大学结束这一节点配对，不是孩子高中毕业或自己的入学日。
vocabulary.example: At the end of college, a person can reflect on that period of life.
